title: Mathematical Reasoning
summary: A statement is a sentence that is either true or false, not both. Commands, questions and opinions are not statements.
~p is true when p is false. 'All A are B' is negated as 'Some A are not B' (or 'Not all A are B'); 'x < 5' as 'x is not less than 5'.
p ∧ q (and) is true only when both are true; p ∨ q (or) is false only when both are false. 'p if and only if q' (p ⇔ q) means both p ⇒ q and q ⇒ p.
Converse: if q then p. Inverse: if not p then not q. Contrapositive: if not q then not p. A statement and its contrapositive are equivalent; the converse need not be true.
'It never rains when it is cold' becomes 'If it is cold, then it never rains'. 'p if q' means 'if q then p'.
By direct method, contrapositive, contradiction, or a counterexample to show a statement false.
mcq: The converse of 'if a number is divisible by 9, then it is divisible by 3' is —
if a number is divisible by 3, then it is divisible by 9
if a number is divisible by 9, then it is not divisible by 3
if a number is not divisible by 3, it is not divisible by 9
if a number is not divisible by 9, then it is also not divisible by 3
A

objective: Write the negation of: (a) The capital of Gujarat is Ahmedabad. (b) All circles are congruent.

(a) The capital of Gujarat is not Ahmedabad.
(b) Some circles are not congruent (not all circles are congruent).
Write the negation of: (i) The number is less than 5. (ii) All prime numbers are odd.

(i) The number is not less than 5.
(ii) Some prime numbers are not odd (e.g. 2).
Write the contrapositive of: (i) If ABCD is a square, then it is a rhombus. (ii) If a and b are rational numbers, then ab is a real number.

(i) If ABCD is not a rhombus, then it is not a square.
(ii) If ab is not a real number, then a and b are not both rational.
Write in the form 'if … then': (a) It never rains when it is cold. (b) A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if its diagonals bisect each other.

(a) If it is cold, then it never rains.
(b) If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, then it is a parallelogram.
objective4: (a) Negate: '√5 is not a rational number.' (b) Converse of 'If x is a prime number, then x is even.' (c) Contrapositive of 'If a number is odd, then its square is not negative.' (d) Combine with 'if and only if': P: if two angles of a triangle are equal, it is isosceles; Q: if a triangle is isosceles, two of its angles are equal.

(a) √5 is a rational number.
(b) If x is even, then x is a prime number.
(c) If the square of a number is negative, then the number is not odd.
(d) A triangle is isosceles if and only if two of its angles are equal.
vsa: Write the converse and contrapositive of 'If a triangle is equilateral, then it is isosceles'.

Converse: if a triangle is isosceles, then it is equilateral (false in general).
Contrapositive: if a triangle is not isosceles, then it is not equilateral (true, equivalent to the original).
